It’s critical that people have someone to call, someone to respond and safe and welcoming options places to go if needed.\n \nThis investment can strengthen vital access to timely support, but it must be part of a nationally system that connects across services and delivers responsive care wherever people are across the country.\n \nWe look forward to seeing the full plan in the coming months, and working with the sector to ensure this investment translates into real, lasting improvements for people and whānau across Aotearoa.\n \nRead the full details of the investment here: https://lnkd.in/edD5p-hk ","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission_govt-announces-10-million-boost-to-mental-activity-7482244289398407168-k784"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Te Hiringa Mahara - Mental Health and Wellbeing Commission","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission"},"datePublished":"2026-07-08T23:23:38.703Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission_childrens-commissioner-appointed-activity-7480763560659304448-6HBh","text":"We welcome the appointment of Jane Searle into her new role as Children's Commissioner from 1 August 2026. Claire, we wish you all the best for your next chapter!\n\nRead more: https://lnkd.in/eResJvCT ","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission_childrens-commissioner-appointed-activity-7480763560659304448-6HBh"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Te Hiringa Mahara - Mental Health and Wellbeing Commission","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission"},"datePublished":"2026-07-06T03:32:13.261Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission_the-final-reading-of-the-mental-health-bill-activity-7479738953223462912-pWna","text":"The final reading of the Mental Health Bill on Saturday 4 July marks a significant step forward to embedding a modern, human rights framework in our mental health and addiction system. \n \nCommenting on the bill’s passage, Sonya Russell, Director Mental Health and Addiction Sector Leadership acknowledged the journey to get here and everyone who has contributed to these changes to mental health law envisioned in the Mental Health and Addiction Inquiry report, He Ara Oranga, published eight years ago.  \n \nThe updated law provides greater human rights protection for people receiving compulsory care. Importantly, through implementation of the law we expect to see a reduction in the use of coercive practices, and better outcomes for people and those who support them. \n \nWe are pleased to see that people under 18 cannot be held in seclusion under this new legislation. \n  \nThere are some areas where the law has not gone as far as we recommended. We will continue to advocate strongly for the elimination of seclusion for adults, and the reduction and eventual phasing out of community compulsory treatment orders that remain sanctioned under the law. \n \nThe law comes into force on 1 July 2028, a year later than initially proposed. A clause is included requiring a comprehensive review of the legislation’s operation and effectiveness within 5 years of its enactment, and every subsequent 5 years.  \n \nImplementation must be properly resourced to enable practice change on the ground to be accelerated. This work will require increased investment in alternative approaches to care and workforce development and training. \n \nAs we turn to next steps, people directly impacted by this law must have the opportunity to be involved in its implementation. This includes Māori, lived experience, and priority population groups, such as Pacific people and disabled people. ","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission_the-final-reading-of-the-mental-health-bill-activity-7479738953223462912-pWna"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Te Hiringa Mahara - Mental Health and Wellbeing Commission","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission"},"datePublished":"2026-06-30T23:29:56.066Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission_the-minister-for-mental-health-hon-matt-doocey-activity-7477866040509784065-aU_o","text":"The Minister for Mental Health Hon Matt Doocey has announced changes to the composition of the Board of Te Hiringa Mahara – Mental Health and Wellbeing Commission.\n\nAfter leading the Board of the initial commission and subsequently being appointed chairperson in 2021, Hayden Wano QSO has not sought reappointment as a board member. He is standing down in early July.\n\nOur new chairperson is current board member Dr Barbara Disley ONZM. Dr Kelly Feng MNZM has been appointed as a new board member.\n\nBarbara joined the Board in July 2023 and was appointed deputy chair in October 2025. She has held significant roles in the mental health and addiction sector over the past 30 plus years, including being a member of the Inquiry into Mental Health and Addiction in 2018.\n\nNew Board member Dr Kelly Feng, Chief Executive for Asian Family Services (AFS), has trained in medicine and social work. Dr Feng has extensive experience in the mental health and addiction field since migrating from China to Aotearoa New Zealand in 2002. She has been appointed on a five-year term. \n\nAcknowledging Hayden's pivotal founding role, Dr Barbara said “the forward looking and solution focused vision he has instilled in the organisation is something we are committed to maintaining”.\n\nTogether, Barbara and Kelly will bring invaluable expertise and leadership to Te Hiringa Mahara as we continue working for better and equitable mental health and wellbeing outcomes for all people in Aotearoa New Zealand.","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission_the-minister-for-mental-health-hon-matt-doocey-activity-7477866040509784065-aU_o"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Te Hiringa Mahara - Mental Health and Wellbeing Commission","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission"},"datePublished":"2026-06-29T02:29:48.733Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission_te-hiringa-mahara-mental-health-and-wellbeing-activity-7477186532508930048-c4_l","text":"Te Hiringa Mahara – Mental Health and Wellbeing Commission has launched a roadmap calling for faster, more focused action to improve mental health, addiction and wellbeing outcomes in Aotearoa New Zealand. \n\nNext Tuesday, we are hosting a one-hour session about this, along with other recent work and what is coming up. This is being hosted by our outgoing Board chair Hayden Wano, and Chief Executive, Karen Orsborn. \n\nAs well as having a chance to hear about recent work by the Commission, this is your chance to ask any questions you've got. \n\nWhen: 3-4pm Tuesday 7 July 2026\nWhere: online Zoom webinar\n\nRVSP: https://lnkd.in/e5MT4S27","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission_te-hiringa-mahara-mental-health-and-wellbeing-activity-7477186532508930048-c4_l"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Te Hiringa Mahara - Mental Health and Wellbeing Commission","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission"},"datePublished":"2026-06-25T03:35:07.275Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission_mental-health-and-wellbeing-is-broad-and-activity-7475753416607277058-ycwn","text":"“Mental health and wellbeing is broad and complex, and we all have our own journeys and experiences. We want people and whānau to receive the support they need earlier, closer to home, and in ways that work for them,” our CE Karen Orsborn said yesterday morning at Parliament.\n\nWe launched a roadmap calling for faster, more focused action to improve mental health, addiction and wellbeing outcomes in Aotearoa New Zealand.\n\nThe event at in the Legislative Council Chamber was hosted by the Cross-Party Mental Health and Addictions Wellbeing Group. We acknowledge contributions from co-chairs Kahurangi Carter and Ingrid Leary, Minister for Mental Health Matt Doocey and mental health advocate Grace Curtis. We also thank Cross-Party Group secretariat Platform Trust for their support. \n\nRead and share the Roadmap for mental health, addiction and wellbeing: www.mhwc.govt.nz/roadmap ","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission_mental-health-and-wellbeing-is-broad-and-activity-7475753416607277058-ycwn"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Te Hiringa Mahara - Mental Health and Wellbeing Commission","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission"},"datePublished":"2026-06-23T23:17:32.527Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission_te-hiringa-mahara-mental-health-and-wellbeing-activity-7475326206788317184-WCDW","text":"Te Hiringa Mahara – Mental Health and Wellbeing Commission- has today launched a roadmap at Parliament calling for faster, more focused action to improve mental health, addiction and wellbeing outcomes in Aotearoa New Zealand.\n\nThe call comes as psychological distress continues to rise across Aotearoa, while the mental health and addiction system struggles to keep pace with people’s needs.\n\nWe acknowledge progress has been made in recent years, but change is not happening fast enough, especially for young people and Māori. \n\nThis roadmap is designed to help decision-makers focus effort and investment where it can make the greatest difference, so people and whānau can get support earlier, closer to home, and in ways that work for them.\n\nWe know mental health is a cross-Government, a whole-of-Government, issue with responsibilities in education, justice, health, and social development. Action needs to be taken to address the broader factors that influence mental health.\n\nThe MHA system can’t do everything on its own, but it must do its part well which is why this Roadmap is focused on the MHA system. \n\nThis roadmap has been shaped by many conversations, engagement activities, and evidence gathered over time. It is grounded in our work over the last five years, and the voices of people with lived experience and communities. We are encouraging people to engage with and share our priorities for a strong mental health system.\n\nRead and download here: www.mhwc.govt.nz/roadmap  ","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission_te-hiringa-mahara-mental-health-and-wellbeing-activity-7475326206788317184-WCDW"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Te Hiringa Mahara - Mental Health and Wellbeing Commission","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission"},"datePublished":"2026-06-18T04:21:28.226Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission_we-hosted-our-system-performance-expert-advisory-activity-7473228365668417536-PQ5C","text":"We hosted our System Performance Expert Advisory Group hui today in Te Whanganui-ā-Tara. It was great to come together with this diverse group of experts from right across the sector who generously shared their rich experience, knowledge and wisdom from a range of perspectives including lived experience, Māori, Pacific, service delivery, clinical and academia. \n\nWith the second system performance ‘report card’ published this week, we acknowledge the input and guidance provided by this group.\n\nIt was a valuable opportunity to discuss our upcoming work programme and seek expert advice on how we can contribute to better and equitable mental health and wellbeing outcomes for people in Aotearoa​.\n\nDiscussions included advice on the design and implementation of our service performance monitoring work and an afternoon sense-making workshop for our upcoming report that aims to better understand how rangatahi and youth are accessing services. \n\nJohn Zonnevylle and Deb Fraser-Komene joined us in the afternoon to help us with the sense-making. Huge thanks to our co-chairs Sharon Shea and Kevin Harper and to Steven Youngblood who facilitated our afternoon session.\n\nPictured from left: \n(back row): Kevin Harper, Ian Soosay, Sharon Shea, Laura Ross, Dean Rangihuna, Richard Woodcock, Catherine Inder, Memo Musa, Leeanne Fisher.\n(front row): Karen Orsborn, Maraea Johns, Alisha Tamepo-Pehi, Tee Siataga, Helen Lockett, Denise Kingi-‘Ulu’ave, Sonya Russell.","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission_we-hosted-our-system-performance-expert-advisory-activity-7473228365668417536-PQ5C"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Te Hiringa Mahara - Mental Health and Wellbeing Commission","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission"},"datePublished":"2026-06-16T02:56:55.833Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission_submissions-on-the-drug-overdose-assistance-activity-7472482314779017216-R66u","text":"Submissions on the Drug Overdose (Assistance Protection) Legislation Bill close tonight. There’s still time to get a submission in on this live-saving piece of legislation.\n\nOur submission focused on three key points:\n- The legislation will reduce overdose fatalities in Aotearoa New Zealand\n- It will support equity of outcomes for Māori\n- It will improve opportunities for contact with services for people experiencing substance use harm.\n\nYou can read the submission on our website here: https://lnkd.in/grbDvpXg \n\nWe encourage you to use any of the information in it to submit your own. ","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission_submissions-on-the-drug-overdose-assistance-activity-7472482314779017216-R66u"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"DiscussionForumPosting","author":{"@type":"Organization","name":"Te Hiringa Mahara - Mental Health and Wellbeing Commission","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission"},"datePublished":"2026-06-15T22:06:44.750Z","mainEntityOfPage":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission_today-te-hiringa-mahara-mental-health-and-activity-7472409287437467648-JtXR","text":"Today Te Hiringa Mahara – Mental Health and Wellbeing Commission has released its latest ‘report card’ on the state of Aotearoa New Zealand’s mental health and addiction system. \n\nThe System performance monitoring report assesses whether people can get help when they need it, where access is not a barrier, the support received is safe and effective, and that we are seeing improved mental health outcomes for people.  \n\nThis 2026 report shows that, while progress has been made overall, it has been inconsistent and the benefits are not reaching people with the highest mental health needs. The system must move faster to meet rising need among young people and Māori. \n\nBased on our assessment of progress, we have made two new recommendations for improvements. We call on Health New Zealand to publish a national seclusion plan by 2027, outlining the pathway to eliminate seclusion, and to the Ministry of Health to expand the collection of outcomes and experience data from people engaging with mental health and addiction services so we can monitor effectiveness of services.\n\nA recommendation first made in June 2024 has been renewed because this has not been realised: we call to Health New Zealand develops an action plan by June 2027 to meet the needs of Māori and whānau accessing specialist mental health and addiction services.\n\nRenewed effort is required by leaders of the mental health and addiction system across all six shifts to improve system performance and address inequities. \n\nRead and share the full report: https://lnkd.in/eTzYNCtK","url":"https://www.linkedin.com/posts/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission_today-te-hiringa-mahara-mental-health-and-activity-7472409287437467648-JtXR"},{"@context":"http://schema.org","@type":"Organization","name":"Te Hiringa Mahara - Mental Health and Wellbeing Commission","url":"https://nz.linkedin.com/company/mental-health-and-wellbeing-commission","address":{"type":"PostalAddress","addressLocality":"Wellington","addressRegion":"Wellington Region","postalCode":"6011","addressCountry":"NZ"},"description":"Te Hiringa Mahara  - Mental Health and Wellbeing Commission is an independent Crown entity, set up under the Mental Health and Wellbeing Commission Act 2020.         " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">The final reading of the Mental Health Bill on Saturday 4 July marks a significant step forward to embedding a modern, human rights framework in our mental health and addiction system. 
 
Commenting on the bill’s passage, Sonya Russell, Director Mental Health and Addiction Sector Leadership acknowledged the journey to get here and everyone who has contributed to these changes to mental health law envisioned in the Mental Health and Addiction Inquiry report, He Ara Oranga, published eight years ago.  
 
The updated law provides greater human rights protection for people receiving compulsory care. Importantly, through implementation of the law we expect to see a reduction in the use of coercive practices, and better outcomes for people and those who support them. 
 
We are pleased to see that people under 18 cannot be held in seclusion under this new legislation. 
  
There are some areas where the law has not gone as far as we recommended. We will continue to advocate strongly for the elimination of seclusion for adults, and the reduction and eventual phasing out of community compulsory treatment orders that remain sanctioned under the law. 
 
The law comes into force on 1 July 2028, a year later than initially proposed. A clause is included requiring a comprehensive review of the legislation’s operation and effectiveness within 5 years of its enactment, and every subsequent 5 years.  
 
Implementation must be properly resourced to enable practice change on the ground to be accelerated. This work will require increased investment in alternative approaches to care and workforce development and training. 
 
As we turn to next steps, people directly impacted by this law must have the opportunity to be involved in its implementation. This includes Māori, lived experience, and priority population groups, such as Pacific people and disabled people. </p>

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Te Hiringa Mahara – Mental Health and Wellbeing Commission- has today launched a roadmap at Parliament calling for faster, more focused action to improve mental health, addiction and wellbeing outcomes in Aotearoa New Zealand.

The call comes as psychological distress continues to rise across Aotearoa, while the mental health and addiction system struggles to keep pace with people’s needs.

We acknowledge progress has been made in recent years, but change is not happening fast enough, especially for young people and Māori. 

This roadmap is designed to help decision-makers focus effort and investment where it can make the greatest difference, so people and whānau can get support earlier, closer to home, and in ways that work for them.

We know mental health is a cross-Government, a whole-of-Government, issue with responsibilities in education, justice, health, and social development. Action needs to be taken to address the broader factors that influence mental health.

The MHA system can’t do everything on its own, but it must do its part well which is why this Roadmap is focused on the MHA system. 

This roadmap has been shaped by many conversations, engagement activities, and evidence gathered over time. It is grounded in our work over the last five years, and the voices of people with lived experience and communities. We are encouraging people to engage with and share our priorities for a strong mental health system.

    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Today Te Hiringa Mahara – Mental Health and Wellbeing Commission has released its latest ‘report card’ on the state of Aotearoa New Zealand’s mental health and addiction system. 

The System performance monitoring report assesses whether people can get help when they need it, where access is not a barrier, the support received is safe and effective, and that we are seeing improved mental health outcomes for people.  

This 2026 report shows that, while progress has been made overall, it has been inconsistent and the benefits are not reaching people with the highest mental health needs. The system must move faster to meet rising need among young people and Māori. 

Based on our assessment of progress, we have made two new recommendations for improvements. We call on Health New Zealand to publish a national seclusion plan by 2027, outlining the pathway to eliminate seclusion, and to the Ministry of Health to expand the collection of outcomes and experience data from people engaging with mental health and addiction services so we can monitor effectiveness of services.

A recommendation first made in June 2024 has been renewed because this has not been realised: we call to Health New Zealand develops an action plan by June 2027 to meet the needs of Māori and whānau accessing specialist mental health and addiction services.

Renewed effort is required by leaders of the mental health and addiction system across all six shifts to improve system performance and address inequities.
